profile.purpose: A shower water test and review of the Taylor Stitch Winslow Parka in mustard waxed cotton. It shows how water-resistant the jacket is and covers its construction, warmth, fit, waxed cotton compared with Barbour, and its main flaw.
profile.thesis: The creator stands in a cold shower for 15 minutes in the Winslow Parka to see how well its waxed cotton keeps water out. Between the test footage he reviews the jacket's materials, the changes from earlier versions, warmth, fit and how its wax compares with Barbour's. He ends on the zipper as its one flaw and a storm flap as the fix.
key_takeaways: The Winslow Parka's shell is organic waxed cotton from Hallie Stevenson, waxed with beeswax. The body lining is 60% wool and 40% nylon, and the sleeves are lined in acetate over polyfill.
The current version fixes two complaints about an earlier one: the scratchy wool-lined sleeves are now acetate-lined, and the sleeves are now gusseted.
In a 15-minute cold shower test the jacket mostly stayed dry, and a note in the chest pocket came out dry. Water got through along the front zipper line.
He suggests adding a storm flap behind or over the zipper to fix the leak.
He says it is not warm enough for a whole winter, despite the website's claim. His estimated range is about 45-50°F up to around 70°F.
It fits true to size with room to layer, and has a straight-cut hem. He is 5'9", about 152 lb, and wears a 38.

He describes the Hallie Stevenson wax as thicker, tougher and more waxy than Barbour's more oily finish. He thinks this makes it closer to waterproof, while Barbour looks more relaxed and is less wrinkly.
He sees the Winslow as better for longer time out in the rain and Barbour as more for short walks. For real all-day outdoor work in rain he would pick a hard shell, rubber or Gore-Tex.

outline.title: Introduction and jacket overview
outline.summary: A cold open from the shower test, then an introduction to the mustard Taylor Stitch Winslow Parka and the story of missing and buying the color. He sets up the shower test and mentions a future Barbour test.

outline.title: Setting up the test and teasing the flaw
outline.summary: He puts a note in the chest pocket, explains why the shower is cold for wax, and sets a timer. He teases a big flaw with an easy fix.

outline.title: Brand context
outline.summary: Taylor Stitch as a small, fast-moving heritage-style brand that releases new products often and keeps improving them. The video is not sponsored.

outline.title: Iteration improvements
outline.summary: Complaints about an earlier Winslow version, namely scratchy wool-lined sleeves and sleeves without gussets. The current version fixes both with acetate lining and gusseted sleeves.

outline.title: Materials and lining
outline.summary: The organic Hallie Stevenson waxed cotton shell, the 60/40 wool-nylon lining and its pilling, and the internal chest pockets, which he would like lined with nylon.

outline.title: Insulation and warmth
outline.summary: The acetate sleeves over polyfill insulation, and the website's 'all winter' warmth claim, which he puts down to San Francisco weather. His own estimated temperature range.

outline.title: Fit
outline.summary: True-to-size fit with structure and room to layer. Straight-cut hem, plus his height, weight and size.

outline.title: Waxed cotton details
outline.summary: Hallie Stevenson's claim that the beeswax-based waxed cotton softens in warm weather and stiffens in cold, and how much of it he can confirm.

outline.title: Taylor Stitch vs Barbour
outline.summary: Barbour as the king of waxed cotton and his fondness for it. Why he finds Barbour jackets impractical, including the hood sold separately.

outline.title: Wax versus oil
outline.summary: An informal comparison of Hallie Stevenson's thicker wax and Barbour's oilier finish: repellency, how each looks and feels, and wrinkling.

outline.title: Practicality
outline.summary: The Winslow is meant for longer outdoor time in rain, while a Barbour is more for brief walks.

outline.title: Test results
outline.summary: He stops after 15 minutes with no sign of the jacket giving out, and credits the wax and the wool lining.

outline.title: Workwear suitability
outline.summary: Whether real outdoor workers would choose waxed cotton over shells, rubber or Gore-Tex. Waxed cotton would eventually wet through in a long downpour.

outline.title: Final verdict and storm flap
outline.summary: The pocket note is dry, but water came in along the zipper line. Water at the neck and sleeves is unavoidable, and he proposes a storm flap as the fix.
